summary: Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring and Ludwig Alsdorf, earning his doctorate and habilitation. He served as a professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991/1994.

Klaus Butzenberger worked in Indology and philosophy, earning degrees at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm. He held teaching posts at Munich, the Free University of Berlin, and Humboldt University before serving as chairholder at the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Fischer worked in Indology and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University, studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea and Ordhendra Coomar Gangoly, and held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (1956–1959) and the University of Bonn (1966–1985).

Klaus Hahlweg specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetan studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich, completing his Ph.D. by 1954 under Helmut Hoffmann, and also studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp.

Klaus Karttunen is an Indologist, historian, and linguist. He studied at the University of Helsinki under scholars including Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. His appointments include positions at the Academy of Finland and several academic posts at the University of Helsinki.

Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt, Göttingen (PhD under Paul Thieme), and Tübingen. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, Göttingen State Library, Tübingen, and was professor of Indology at Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Matzel worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, Jena, Humboldt, the Free University of Berlin (Ph.D.), and Würzburg. He taught at Berlin and Peradeniya before serving as professor of Germanic philology at the University of Regensburg (1968–1989).

Klaus Mylius was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Friedrich Weller and Karl Ammer at Halle-Wittenberg and Leipzig. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig (1970–1991), Bayreuth, Göttingen, and Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and held a postdoctoral teaching post there in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg, and Giessen under scholars including Annemarie von Gabain, holding professorships at the University of Giessen (1972) and Göttingen (1992–2003).

Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied at the University of Bonn under Paul Hacker and completed his PhD at the University of Münster. He spent his career at Münster as an assistant, lecturer, and ordinary professor from 1980.

Klaus Strunk was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Hoffmann. He served on the faculty at Saarland University from around 1968 to 1977 and at the University of Munich from approximately 1977 to 1998.

Klaus Wille is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. His career includes work at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997) and multiple research positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2026).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Bonn, Marburg (Ph.D. under Michael Hahn), and Hamburg, he held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, Hamburg, the University of Vienna (2010), and Hong Kong (2023).

Klaus-Josef Notz specialized in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Philosophisch-Theologische Hochschule Benediktbeuern and the University of Munich, where he earned a Doctor theologiae in 1984 and later served as a lecturer in 1996.

Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy degree at Uppsala University by 2000, where he studied under the supervision of Peter Schalk.

Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He held professorships at the University of Oslo and the University of Bergen (1996).

Knut Kristiansen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo under Georg Morgenstierne. He later served as a university lecturer in Modern Indian languages at the University of Oslo from 1971 to 1998.

Kobun Otogawa was a Buddhist studies practitioner-scholar educated at Komazawa University, Kyoto University (under Gadjin Nagao), and Eihei-ji. He studied under Kodo Sawaki and held teaching posts at Tassajara, Haiku Zendo, and Naropa University.

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership roles at Komazawa University between 1892 and 1909 and taught at the University of Tokyo.
